title: Place an order

entry.label: POST /orders
entry.trigger: A signed-in customer submits the checkout form

summary: A signed-in customer posts a sku and a quantity. The guard checks the session, the controller validates the body, the service inserts the row, emails a receipt and fans out an order.placed event, and the client gets the stored order back with 201.

files.role: Parses the body, calls the service

hops.title: POST /orders is wired to requireAuth, then createOrder
hops.why: Hono runs the handler list left to right, so requireAuth has to call next() before createOrder is ever reached.

hops.title: requireAuth refuses a request with no session
hops.why: The session was put on the context upstream; this guard only reads it, copies the user across and lets the chain continue.

hops.title: createOrder parses the body and calls the service once
hops.why: HTTP glue only: Zod parses, one service call, the envelope wraps the answer with 201.

hops.title: createOrderSchema is the shape the body must have
hops.why: sku must be non-empty and quantity a positive integer; CreateOrderInput is inferred from this object, so the service's parameter type cannot drift from what was validated.

hops.title: placeOrder inserts the row, then emails and notifies
hops.why: The insert comes first, so a backordered sku still leaves a row behind before OutOfStock is thrown.

throws.when: the inserted row came back with backordered = true

hops.title: insertOrder writes one row and returns it
hops.why: One tagged-template insert with returning *, so the service gets the stored row, defaults included.

hops.title: sendReceipt emails the customer through Resend
hops.why: A leaf: the request leaves the process here, and nothing on this path reads the provider's answer.

hops.title: notify picks its handlers at runtime
hops.why: Every registered key that prefixes the event name gets the payload, in registration order, so the code alone does not say which functions run next.
hops.reason: handlers is filled at boot and matched by prefix; today two keys prefix order.placed, and a third registration would change the answer without touching this file

pseudocode.text: Refuse the request unless a session is on it
Validate sku and quantity from the body
Insert the order row and read it back
Refuse with OutOfStock when the row came back backordered
Email the receipt, then hand the event to every handler whose key prefixes order.placed
Answer 201 with the stored order in the envelope

branches.name: no session
branches.outcome: Unauthorized is thrown; the error handler answers 401

branches.name: backordered
branches.outcome: OutOfStock is thrown after the row was already inserted

failure.title: A body with quantity 0
steps: createOrderSchema.parse throws a ZodError inside createOrder
the error handler answers 400 with the issues
placeOrder never runs, so nothing is inserted and no email goes out

decisions.text: The row is inserted before the stock check, so a backorder is recorded rather than refused up front.
decisions.alternative: Checking stock first would need a second query and would still race with other orders.

questions.q: Where does user.id come from by the time placeOrder reads it?
questions.a: requireAuth copies session.user onto the context, and the controller reads it back with c.get('user').

questions.q: What has already been written when OutOfStock is thrown?
questions.a: The order row: the throw happens after insertOrder returned.

questions.q: Why is the last hop unresolved?
questions.a: notify matches handlers by key prefix at runtime; two registrations answer today, so the page names both instead of guessing one.
